newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says Israel wants to destroy peace deals.
newsitem.headline: PLO says Israel wants to destroy peace deals.

text.p: A Palestinian leader accused Israel on Sunday of systematically aiming to scrap peace deals and gradually implement a plan to deprive Palestinians of self-determination on their land.

"The plan of the current Israeli government is to reach an unjust settlement with the Palestinians. It is to give Palestinians limited administrative powers but no control over the land," Palestinian Information and Culture Minister Yasser Abed-Rabbo told reporters.

"Israel has started to implement this plan by gradually destroying the PLO-Israeli peace deals through land confiscations, building settlements and by demolishing Palestinian houses in areas not under its civilian jurisdiction."

U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk, speaking later to the U.S.-Israel Chamber of Commerce, said that the framework interim 1993 peace deal reached at Oslo between the Palestine Liberation Organisation and Israel's former government had foundered.
"The core bargain of Oslo has broken down -- Israel was promised security and the Palestinians were promised self-government," Indyk said, as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu listened.
"Terrorism on the one side and unilateral acts which have created the impression that the final status issues are being pre-empted on the other have combined to break this trust."
Netanyahu said trust resided in keeping deals and he accused the Palestinians of violating accords he said Israel observed.

Netanyahu came to power reluctant to carry out Israeli-PLO peace deals agreed by the previous Labour-led government. Peace talks were halted in March after he started building a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem, which Israel occupied in 1967 and later annexed.
Several days after work began on the settlement, a Palestinian militant opposed to the interim peace deals killed himself and three Israelis when he bombed a Tel Aviv cafe.

Top Palestinian negotiator Mahmoud Abbas, better known as Abu Mazen, said Netanyahu's government was returning to a formula of earlier Likud prime minister Menachem Begin as part of the Camp David accords in 1978 with Egypt, which the Palestinians rejected.
"That proposal gave Palestinians limited powers to administer themselves but no control over the land," Abbas told Reuters. "An occupier has no right to build on Palestinian occupied land."
Palestinian officials said Israel had plans, amounting to a policy of ethnic cleansing likely to spark violence, to demolish 500 Palestinian homes in the West Bank.
"These actions are leading to mounting Palestinian frustration which could spark popular violence directed not only against Israel but also against the Palestinian Authority," Abed Rabbo said.
"Palestinians only see land confiscations, building of settlements, house demolitions and a weak Authority. This will lead to a great explosion with dire consequences"
An Israeli official confirmed that hundreds of homes were built without permits but a spokesman insisted that anyone facing the demolition of property could still challenge the order.

"The policy of the government and the defence establishment is to impose law and order and to deal with violations of the law by both Arabs and Jews," Israel's defence ministry said, adding that there was no "known plan" to demolish 500 homes.
